statement.text:
(a) Are there integral homology spheres with arbitrarily large (integral) Dehn
surgery number? Are there irreducible examples? Does the connected sum
of $n$ nontrivial homology spheres have Dehn surgery number at least $n$?
(b) Given a 3-manifold $Y$ with a smooth orientation-preserving $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sym-
metry $\varphi$, Sakuma [Sak01] (generalizing [PS01]) proved that $Y$ admits a
surgery description compatible with the symmetry. Define the equivariant
(integral) Dehn surgery number of $(Y, \varphi)$ as the minimal number of con-
nected components of any such link. Do there exist $(Y, \varphi)$ whose equivari-
ant (integral) Dehn surgery number is arbitrarily larger than the (integral)
Dehn surgery number?
(c) Following the remarks below, we can consider the following specific case:
Does there exist a manifold with a 2-fold symmetry whose equivariant
(integral) Dehn surgery number is larger than the (integral) Dehn surgery
number?
